source_text: Noluit - inquit - nominare concupiscentiam carnis, quae non est a Patre, sed ex mundo est; cuius mundi princeps dictus est diabolus: qui eam in Domino non invenit, quia Dominus homo non per ipsam ad homines venit [n27] . Verbis ergo ipsius Manichaei, concupiscentiam carnis non a Deo factam, sed a mundo, cuius tamen mundi principem diabolum dicis, conditam profiteris.
pass_a_gloss: He was unwilling — he says — to name the desire of the flesh, which is not from the Father but is from the world; of which world the devil has been called prince: who did not find it in the Lord, because the Lord as a human being did not come to humans through it. By the words therefore of Manichaeus himself you profess that the desire of the flesh was not made by God, but was founded by the world, of which world nevertheless you say the devil is prince.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: “He was unwilling,” he says, “to name the desire of the flesh, which is not from the Father but from the world. The devil is called the ruler of this world. He did not find this desire in the Lord, because the Lord came among human beings as a man without it” (Augustine, On Marriage and Concupiscence 2.5.14; compare 1 John 2:16; John 14:30). In the very words of Manichaeus, then, you profess that the desire of the flesh was made not by God but by the world, whose ruler you nevertheless say is the devil.

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
